messages.content: Help me apply a function named 'processType' to each type in a union type object named 'unionTypeObj' to analyze its properties?

function.name: forEachType
function.description: This function iterates over each type in a given type object, applying a specified function to it. If the type object represents a union of types, the function is applied to each type in the union; otherwise, it is applied directly to the single type. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

type.description: The type object, potentially representing a union of types. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

f.description: The function to apply to each type in the type object. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that shows two ways to run `processType()` against every member of a TypeScript “union” type object (`unionTypeObj`).  
Feel free to copy/paste into your project – adjust the names/structure to match your own data.

---

### 1️⃣  Using the **tool** (`forEachType`)  

```js
// Assume this is already defined somewhere else:
// const unionTypeObj = {...};          // Your union type description
// function processType(t){ … }        // What you want to do per type

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Call the built‑in helper so it walks the union automatically.
 *
 * NOTE: 
 * - `type`: Must be a *string* containing the serialized form of the
 *           union type object (e.g., JSON).
 * - `f`:     A *JavaScript source string* that defines the callback
 *            function.  It receives one argument – the current type’s
 *            key/name from the union.
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
await functions.forEachType({
  type: JSON.stringify(unionTypeObj),      // <-- serialize the whole object
  f: processType.toString()               // <-- turn the fn into text
});

/*
Example result (if unionTypeObj has keys "A", "B" & "C"):

> Processing A
> Processing B
> Processing C
*/
```

#### Why stringify?

The tool expects plain strings, so serializing guarantees no accidental reference sharing between calls.  
When you deserialize inside `processType`, you’ll get back the original value.

---

### 2️⃣  Manual implementation (no external tool)

If you prefer to keep everything in vanilla JavaScript / Node.js, here’s a tiny utility that does essentially the same thing:

```js
/**
 * Walks all members of a union-type descriptor and applies a callback.
 *
 * @param {object} unionObj  An object whose top‑level keys represent individual types.
 *                           Example: `{ A:{…}, B:{…}, C:{…} }`.
 * @param {(key:string)=>void} cb Callback invoked once per key/value pair.
 */
function walkUnionTypes(unionObj, cb){
  Object.entries(unionObj)
         .filter(([k])=> typeof k === 'string')   // guard against non-string keys
         .forEach( ([key,val]) => cb(key, val) );
}

/* Usage ----------------------------------------------------------- */

walkUnionTypes(unionTypeObj, (typeKey, typeDef)=>{
  // You now have both the key ("A") and the full definition ({…})
  processType({ key:typeKey, def:typeDef });
});

```

This pattern gives you complete control—useful if you need more context (like the entire definition) during processing.

---

### Quick sanity check

Whichever method you pick, make sure:

| ✅ | Check |
|---|-------|
| ✔️ | `unionTypeObj` really contains a flat map of type definitions (not nested arrays etc.). |
| ✔️ | `processType` accepts whatever shape you’re passing (just a key vs. key+definition). |
| ✔️ | For the tool version, remember to await the promise returned by `functions.forEachType`.

Happy coding! 🚀
